title: Water quality and regulatory compliance
summary: Chlorine residual decays below the action level at one reservoir while a second reservoir's analyser silently fails. Edge IQ must escalate the first and NOT escalate the second - telling a real excursion apart from a dead instrument.

iqLayers.fabricIq: Chlorine residual series and the compliance rollup per site.
iqLayers.foundryIq: Residual action levels, sampling obligations and the reporting SOP.
iqLayers.workIq: Regulator correspondence and the compliance calendar.

seededFault.behaviour: Decays to 0.14 mg/L, breaching the 0.2 mg/L action level on 3 days.
seededFault.why: A genuine excursion. Residual falls, then sits pinned at its floor - flat, but flat at a breach level.

secondFault.behaviour: Reports exactly 0.52 mg/L for 3 straight days - zero variance.
secondFault.why: A dead analyser, not a water quality event. 0.52 is comfortably in range, so a naive threshold alarm sees nothing at all while the utility is flying blind on that reservoir.

designNote: The classifier requires invariant readings AND zero breaches before calling an analyser suspect. Without the second condition, RES-03's genuine breach - which is also invariant, because a decayed residual sits on its floor - gets dismissed as an instrument fault. That is the failure mode that matters: it would suppress a real public health event. The rule lives in infra/scripts/seed/seed_cosmos.py -> shape_compliance().

script.ask: Did any chlorine residual breach compliance limits in the last 30 days, and which sites were affected?
script.expect: Routes to water-quality. Reports RES-03 with 3 breach days, cites the action level from the knowledge base.
script.watchFor: RES-07 must NOT appear as a breach. It has no breaches - it has no real readings at all.

script.ask: Is the chlorine analyser at RES-07 reporting correctly, or do we have an instrument fault?
script.expect: Flags RES-07 as a suspect analyser: 4 suspect days, invariant readings, no breaches. Recommends calibration, not a water quality escalation.
script.watchFor: This is the interesting answer. The value is in range, so nothing alarmed - the fault is the absence of variation, which only shows up if you look for it.

script.ask: What are our reporting obligations for the RES-03 excursion, and by when?
script.expect: Foundry IQ returns the notification SOP with timescales.
script.watchFor: Citations should be regulatory documents, and the classification badges should show the governance ceiling being applied.

script.ask: Summarise both issues for the duty manager, separating what is a water quality risk from what is an instrument problem.
script.expect: One briefing that keeps the two cases distinct and recommends different actions for each.
script.watchFor: Conflating them is the failure. One needs a tanker and a notification; the other needs a technician with a calibration kit.

talkingPoints: Threshold alarms miss a stuck sensor entirely - the reading looks healthy. Edge IQ reasons about the shape of the signal, not just its value.
The distinction is deliberately hard: both signals are flat. Only the breach count separates them.
Getting this wrong in the safe direction still costs you - a suppressed excursion is a public health failure, not a false positive.
